title: 3-2-1: On making adjustments, criticism, and improvement
author: James Clear
summary: This is James Clear's weekly 3-2-1 newsletter format presenting three ideas from the author, two quotes from others, and one question for contemplation. Clear's three ideas focus on: improvement as being better than your past self (not comparing against others), taking things seriously without taking them personally (responding to criticism without digesting it), and aiming as an adjustable process throughout life rather than just at the start. The two quotes include wisdom from Baba Hari Dass on teaching to learn, and Alan Kay's reminder that our perceptions are limited like a frog's brain. The closing question asks whether you're building or maintaining. This short-form newsletter distills actionable wisdom and philosophical reflection into digestible form.
points: Improvement is being better than your past self, not comparing against others; keep the focus internal and measure progress against your own trajectory. You can take things seriously without taking them personally; respond to criticism by taking what's useful and leaving the rest rather than defending. Aiming is something you can do throughout the process in most areas of life; pick a direction and start moving, learning and refining along the way. Teaching in order to learn is a powerful principle that deepens understanding through explanation and communication. You can't truly learn to see until you realize you are blind—your perception is limited like a frog's brain which only sees moving oblong objects.
quotes: Improvement is being better than your past self. It doesn't have to be more complicated than that.
You can take things seriously without taking them personally.
The frog only sees a little of the world we see, but it still thinks it perceives the whole world. Now, of course, we are not like frogs! Or are we?
